title.narrative: No. of countries that use MAPS II

description.narrative: No. of countries that use MAPS II

comment.narrative: By 2019 MAPS Secretariat is operational. By 2019 at least 2 new MAPS II modules developed MAPS II tool tested and piloted in at least 3 countries. Implementation mechanisms for the MAPS Secretariat will depend on MAPS operational setup and on additional funding being secured for the MDTF. The key risk is the lack of a timely decision from the MAPS working group since interested donors are keen to see the operationalsetup of MAPS before committing funds for this purpose. More coordination and resources for MAPS rollout increases the likelihood of uptake from countries.
at least 20 countries have used MAPS II

MAPS assessments have been conducted in 15 countries including Bangladesh India and Kazakhstan which have led to meaningful reforms. Additionally seven of these assessments have been certified by the MAPS Secretariat as of August 2024 ensuring their compliance with international standards. Ongoing support has also facilitated the implementation of recommendations from these assessments such as legal amendments in Kazakhstan based on MAPS findings.Specific examples highlight the initiatives impact further. Pilot projects for MAPS Supplementary Modules have been initiated including professionalization assessments in Senegal and sectoral assessments for road and water sectors in Ethiopia. Furthermore action plans based on MAPS recommendations have been developed in countries like TimorLeste Lebanon and Djibouti leading to concrete reforms in public procurement systems.

comment.narrative: Insufficient demand for a GPPtype body due to competing interests or difficulty finding host institution outside the World Bank. The WB will act as interim secretariat and the GPP will be coordinated in a deliberately participatory and collegial fashion to ensure early ownership and demand from stakeholders.

The GPP Body grant implementation was affected by COVID19 and it resulted in delays on delivering thestocktaking study on public procurement and the consultation and communications plans had to be adaptedto the new context.Update at the time of finalizing this Report April 2022 The report was released in January 2022 at a virtualevent that gathered almost 400 participants from international organizations private sector academics andprocurement professionals. The main purpose of the stocktaking was to identify the key issuesneeds thatwould help shape the focus and formation of the body. The reaction to the publication of the Report has beenoverwhelmingly positive. As of February 2022 the report has been downloaded over 1500 times. There hasbeen a flood of mentions on social media news outlets such as Bloomberg Linea in Latin America and froma range of sources and authors including by The WB President David Malpass and the World Bank GroupsSenior Management Team. There has been mention of the Report by external organizations and individualsin published blogs and posts as well.team expects now to implement the communications strategy and continue with the dissemination andpromotion of the report and the Global Partnership. The team has also planned for the coming monthsseveral consultation meetings on the governance and sustainability of the GPP. GPP is planned to beestablished by Q4. There is a potential risk of not having enough funds to establish the GPP nonetheless theteam is in the process of assuring financial partners.

title.narrative: Documented instances of stakeholder engagement leading to efficiency and corruption fixes

description.narrative: Documented instances of stakeholder engagement leading to efficiency and corruption fixes

comment.narrative: Transparency and citizen participation on procurement are often seen as second order reforms due to insufficient systematic evidence on concrete impact in these areas. The MDTF must be open to a neutral assessment of what the real outcomes of this type of work are in making funding decisions. For this reason during the first phase emphasis will be put on research and documenting effective models for stakeholder participation that seek to validate the hypothesis of the value added by these interventions and will form the basis for some funding decisions in the second phase of the program. Client countries must also drive thesereforms in order to attain success therefore clear incentives for governments must be articulated by Bank teams leading the activities
By the end of the program at least 5 documented instances of effective stakeholder engagement of which 1 is citizen participation 1 private sectorPPP 1 government open data andor analytics

description.narrative: Outcome 2: Development of Country Capacities for Better Procurement Systems

title.narrative: No. of government procurement systems with increased competition

description.narrative: No. of government procurement systems with increased competition

comment.narrative: By the end of the program at least 6 countries 2 LICs 2 MICs 2 FCS with more competitive procurement

The GPP MDTF has supported 12 countries in reforming their procurement frameworks leading to an environment that encourages greater participation particularly from small and mediumsized enterprises SMEs. For instance in Malawi the implementation of an emarketplace platform aimed to improve access for SMEs which is expected to increase competition among bidders. Similarly in Tanzania a capacitybuilding program focused on empowering womenled SMEs to participate in procurement processes thereby broadening the competitive landscape.While specific data on the actual increase in competition is limited qualitative feedback suggests that these reforms led to more bidders participating in procurement opportunities. For example the establishment of an eprocurement system in Burkina Faso streamlined the bidding process which is likely to attract a wider range of bidders.Although precise metrics on competition increases may be lacking the initiatives implemented have laid the groundwork for a more competitive procurement environment. Continued efforts will be necessary to sustain these improvements and further promote competitive practices in public procurement.

description.narrative: Outcome 3: Systematic Learning and Research on Impact of Procurement Reform Approaches

title.narrative: No. of crosscountry knowledge sharing

description.narrative: No. of crosscountry knowledge sharing

comment.narrative: By 2020 at least 2 crosscountry knowledgesharing events. By the end of the program at least 1 regionalglobal mechanism for knowledgesharing established in addition to GPP

The GPP MDTF facilitated several crosscountry knowledgesharing initiatives significantly enhancing public procurement systems. For instance Bangladesh shared its best practices from the impact evaluation of its eprocurement system with Uganda helping the latter improve its procurement processes. Kazakhstans MAPS assessments provided valuable insights that India utilized to strengthen its procurement framework. Similarly Indias experiences with eprocurement informed Malawis approach streamlining its procurement processes. Malawis establishment of an emarketplace served as a model for improving SME access in Gabon demonstrating effective knowledge transfer. Additionally Gabons research on barriers faced by SMEs was shared with Ivory Coast guiding policies to enhance SME participation in procurement. Tanzanias capacitybuilding programs aimed at empowering womenled SMEs were shared with Kenya promoting similar initiatives in that country. Lastly Ethiopias experience in developing robust legal frameworks for procurement reforms served as a guide for Senegal in enhancing its own systems.
